S21.01.note: The language word is written from the fence language (the span shows {language}), so the tester sees the language the model wrote in the fence, not a fixed label.
steps: Send a message in the chat that asks for a short Python script
Wait for the answer to finish and look at the code block that appears
Read the header bar at the top of the code block
Compare the word at the left of the header with the language of the code
S21.01.where: Ask in chat for code in any language, so the answer has a code block; the header bar of the block shows the language name (for example python) on the left, next to the buttons 'Copy', 'Edit', download and 'Expand code'

S21.02.note: Highlighting is done by HighlightedCode and shikiHighlighter; there is no control. It is turned off while the answer is still streaming.
steps: Send a message in the chat that asks for a short Python script with a comment and a string
Look at the colours of keywords, strings and comments in the code block
Compare with Expected: code should be coloured by its language
S21.02.where: Inside any code block in an answer; colours come from the block's highlighter

S21.03.note: The button changes to 'Copied' for about 2 seconds, and to 'Copy failed' if the clipboard is blocked. The visible text 'Copy' comes from the default value of markdown.copy in the code.
steps: Send a message in the chat that asks for a short Python script
Click the 'Copy' button in the top bar of the code block
Paste into a text field (for example the message box) with Command+V
Compare the pasted text with the code in the block: it should match exactly, with no extra header or line numbers
S21.03.where: Any code block in an answer > 'Copy' button in the block header bar (tooltip-free text button; its accessible name is 'Copy code')

S21.04.note: The file name comes from codeFileName.ts; the tooltip is the literal template 'Download {{fileName}}' filled with the file name.
steps: Send a message in the chat that asks for a short Python script
Hover over the download icon in the code block header and read the tooltip
Click the download icon
Open the downloaded file and check its extension matches the language (for example .py for Python)
S21.04.where: Any code block in an answer > download icon in the header bar (no visible words; hover shows the name 'Download' followed by the file name, for example 'Download script.py')

S21.08.note: The dialog title uses the template '{{language}} code'.
steps: Send a message in the chat that asks for a long Python script
Hover over the expand icon and read the tooltip 'Expand code'
Click the expand icon
Look for the full-screen dialog with the title like 'python code', the code, and the 'Close expanded code' icon at the top right
S21.08.where: Any code block in an answer > expand icon in the header bar (tooltip 'Expand code'); it opens a large dialog titled with the language followed by 'code'

S21.09.note: The highlighting is in the DiffLines component of CodeBlock.tsx, which only runs for fence language 'diff'. The separate artifact changes view (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactChangesView.tsx) was not walked through; its path is not confirmed from the chat.
steps: Send a message in the chat that asks for a short unified diff of a code change, in a diff code block
Look at the code block with the lines that start with + and -
Check that added lines have a green background and removed lines have a red background
Compare with Expected: changed lines are highlighted
S21.09.where: Send a message that asks for a diff, so the answer has a code block whose fence language is 'diff' (lines starting with + and -); the lines are coloured green for added and red for removed

S21.10.note: Formatting is DiffLines plus the syntax highlighter for diff; no separate hunk header control was found in the code.
steps: Send a message in the chat that asks for a diff of a small change
Look at the diff block: each line should be on its own row with + or - at the start
Check that hunk header lines (starting with @@) are readable in the block
S21.10.where: Same as S21.09: a code block whose fence language is 'diff' in an answer; the lines show the +/- diff formatting

S21.12.needs: a model that can run code (Auto works); deployment must have code execution switched on (see note)
S21.12.note: The '+' button's exact label was not confirmed in the code. Running needs the e2b execution gate on (AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 and E2B_API_KEY, apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts); the plan says this is not yet switched on.
steps: Open the message box in the chat
Open the '+' menu next to the message box
Click 'Run code' to turn it on
Send a message that asks for a Python calculation
Look for the 'Code Execution' block under the answer and check that it shows 'Running Python…' and then the result
S21.12.where: Message box > the '+' menu (the plus button, exact label not confirmed in code) > 'Run code' toggle row

S21.13.needs: a signed-in account; the Code page for the account
S21.13.note: Runtime choice is in CodeComposer.tsx (the select with CODE_COPY.defaultRuntimeOption). The exact visible heading text and the path to the Code page were not fully confirmed; the select is not the chat code-run runtime.
steps: Open the Code page of the app
Open the environment section of the new task form
Open the select field for the environment
Compare the options: default runtime plus coding harness and image groups
S21.13.where: The /code page (Code workspace), in the environment select field: the first option is the default runtime, followed by optgroups for coding harnesses and images

S21.15.needs: a model that can run code and an execution gate that is on
S21.15.note: Output only shows when the run produced stdout; the execution gate is not yet switched on per the plan.
steps: Turn on 'Run code' in the '+' menu
Send a message that asks for code that prints a line of text
Click the 'Code Execution' block header if it is collapsed
Look for the 'Output' label and the printed text in a monospace box
S21.15.where: After a code run in the chat (see S21.12), the 'Code Execution' block under the answer > 'Output' section

S21.16.needs: a model that can run code and an execution gate that is on
S21.16.note: The red colour is the destructive text token in the same file.
steps: Turn on 'Run code' in the '+' menu
Send a message that asks for Python code that raises an error
Look at the 'Code Execution' block under the answer
Check that the 'Stderr' label and its box are shown in red, separate from 'Output'
S21.16.where: After a code run that writes to error output, in the 'Code Execution' block under the answer > 'Stderr' section (red label)

S21.18.needs: a model that can run code and an execution gate that is on
S21.18.note: A successful run shows only the tick icon, with no text.
steps: Turn on 'Run code' in the '+' menu
Send a message that asks for Python code that calls exit with the number 3
Look at the 'Code Execution' header icon: it should be a cross
Read the text 'Exit code: 3' inside the block and compare with Expected
S21.18.where: The 'Code Execution' block under an answer: the status icon in its header (a tick for success, a cross for failure) and the text 'Exit code:' when the code failed

S21.19.needs: a paid account that allows file creation (not confirmed); no file to upload
S21.19.note: The chip's own visible text was not found; the rendering is in MessageBubble.tsx (generated files block) and downloadGeneratedFile. Plan requirements for the account were not confirmed.
steps: Open the '+' menu next to the message box
Choose 'Office files' and pick an output format
Send a message that asks for a small spreadsheet
Look under the answer for the generated file: an image preview, a spreadsheet preview, or a download chip with the file name
Click the file and check that it opens or downloads
S21.19.where: Chat '+' menu > 'Office files' (option to create files), then the answer shows a generated file as a download chip or preview under the answer

S21.20.needs: a model that can run code and an execution gate that is on
S21.20.note: Images are shown only for the allowed image types (gif, jpeg, png, webp).
steps: Turn on 'Run code' in the '+' menu
Send a message that asks for a Python script that plots a sine wave with matplotlib and saves it as a PNG image
Look at the 'Code Execution' block under the answer
Check that the label 'Plot 1' is shown above a picture of the chart
S21.20.where: After a code run that draws a chart (see S21.12), the 'Code Execution' block shows a 'Plot 1' label and the image under the answer

S21.21.note: No retry control was found in CodeExecutionBlock.tsx or in apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts. The 'Retry' button in MessageBubble.tsx regenerates the answer, not the run. The plan marks this partial.

Click 'Capabilities' in the Settings list
Find the section 'Code execution and file creation'
Read the line under the switch: 'Run code and create files in a sandbox that can reach only GitHub, npm and PyPI.' and compare with Expected
S21.29.where: Settings > Capabilities > 'Code execution and file creation' (switch 'Cloud code execution and file creation')
